cells.tense: Right now you can be close to someone without losing the shape of what you are moving toward.
cells.ask: Tell one person one true thing about how the work is actually going, then go back to it. Notice you did not have to leave either one.
cells.core:
You can be with someone and still be headed somewhere. That is harder than it sounds, and you are doing it — the person in front of you gets your real attention, and your own direction does not dissolve while you give it. You are not absorbing them and you are not steering them.

What makes it work is that you are not holding on. You stay with them while they are there, and when the conversation ends you go back to your own road without either one costing you the other. That costs something to keep: it means staying present when it would be easier to perform, and getting your own goals named when attention feels generous. You carry weight and you keep going — that is what is holding this together. It does not need to be forced. It is already running.
cells.sheetLine: You can be close and still be moving where you meant to go.
cells.verb: feeling with someone rather than only about them
cells.place: in the motion toward what you are trying to finish

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead you are already bracing for a version of this that has not happened yet, and it is pulling you out of the room you are standing in.
cells.ask: Finish the one thing that is actually done and stop carrying its ending as a maybe. Say the ending out loud to yourself once, then leave the next step for tomorrow.
cells.core:
You are carrying other people's weight before they hand it to you. Goals you have, and other people's feelings get folded into them until you cannot tell which momentum is yours. You move on behalf of others and call it direction, and the thing you were actually aiming at drifts.

The version you are bracing for is not the one in front of you. You are already solving a conversation that has not started, already softening an ending that has not arrived. That is not care; it is rehearsal, and it costs you the present. What ends here needs to be let end — not crushed, just finished — so the next thing has somewhere to begin. Endings you honor make room. Endings you postpone run the whole show.
cells.sheetLine: You are pushing ahead on a road that is not entirely yours.

cells.tense: Back at some point spending feeling made the going impossible, so you stopped feeling it, and you are still standing at that door though you have already walked through it.
cells.ask: Pick one person you see most days and ask them one plain question about their week. Let the answer land before you decide what it means.
cells.core:
You keep your distance and tell yourself it is efficiency. People come and go around you and nothing sticks, not because you are cold but because arriving fully would slow the thing you are chasing. The contact stays at the surface and you have stopped expecting more.

What is missing is not warmth and it is not effort. It is the small ongoing work of adjusting — sensing what actually helps here, what to add, what to leave out — and that work has gone quiet. Feeling into someone will not come back by trying harder at it. It comes back through attention: noticing, correcting, staying in the exchange instead of managing it from a step back. Start small. One person, one real question, and let yourself be in it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep people at the surface so the going stays clear.

cells.tense: Right now you are doing things that land as warmth on other people while it registers in you as nothing in particular.
cells.ask: Take one thing you did this week that someone else called kind and say plainly what you were thinking in that moment. Do not correct it into something warmer than it was.
cells.core:
People feel something from you that you would not describe as feeling. You listen, you hold a line for someone, you make a decision gentler than it had to be — and your own account of it is just that it was the sensible thing to do. The connection reaches them. It does not reach you.

The shape of it is not hidden from you; you know how you move and you know what usually works. What has not been claimed is the source. You are attributing your own motion to the situation, to what was needed, to the practical read. Naming it as yours does not make it softer or needier. It just puts the doing back with the one who is doing it. Start with one action, not the pattern.
cells.sheetLine: They feel your care. You have not said it was yours.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that others already feel a connection the person does not — the record gives the shape, not a fact about any particular room. A reader could rightly say it is not indifference, only patience or exhaustion, and the read would still stand. The asks survive a wrong read because each one can be done whether or not the read holds, and the sentence that serves me more than the person is the one about others feeling warmth they can't feel — so I have kept it narrow and made it something they can refuse.
